The label is the maintainer's, not this seat's assessment of the card.

Per `pm-dispatch` SKILL.md the label reorders selection only — **优先是排序,不是豁免**; the claim protocol and the same-file serial queue are not waived.

**One constraint that p0 does not relax, flagged because this card is the one that touches it:** the work lands in `content/docs/releases/`, which CLAUDE.md governs —

> Release notes are written **centrally, at release time** — not accreted one PR at a time. […] If you believe a releases page has a factual error, file an issue or make it a **dedicated docs-only PR** — never a rider on code changes.

A dedicated docs-only PR is the sanctioned route and is what #8882 took one release earlier. What p0 must not turn this into is a rider on some other change to get it landed faster. The urgency is real; the surface is still governed.

Sibling #10229 is also p0 and touches disjoint files (`content/docs/deployment/*`), so the two can run in parallel with no serial-queue contention.

## ⛔ The approval, verbatim, and its exact scope

`content/docs/releases/**` is **RELEASE-OWNED**. This lane's standing rule allows exactly two channels: a **factual error** may go through a dedicated docs-only PR, and a **completeness gap** requires **per-card maintainer approval** and ⛔ **does not constitute a precedent**.

Authoring the missing 17.1.0 section is a completeness gap. I asked for that approval and the maintainer gave it, verbatim:

> 补写 17.1.0 章节 已经有issue，插队处理

⇒ **This card is approved. The rule is not relaxed.** ⛔ The next releases-page completeness gap needs its own approval; this comment is not a precedent to cite. Recording it here because an approval that lives only in a chat session is an approval that cannot be audited.

⚠️ Concurrency note: this is the **4th** in flight against a maintainer-set cap of 3, taken as a queue-jump on the same footing as `priority:p0`. Both p0s in this round are release-facing.

## 裁决 (rulings)

Items 1–3 of the card's suggested shape, which it correctly calls mechanical against a convention already on the page:

1. **Author the 17.1.0 section** on `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx`, following the **v16 page's treatment of 16.1** — that is the established shape, not an invented expectation.
2. **Update the "Release status" blockquote** so it names the current `latest`. It currently reads *"17.0.0 is released… published to the `latest` tag on 2026-08-14"* — true, but no longer the whole truth.
3. **Update `releases/index.mdx`'s v17 parenthetical** — `(current series: 17.0.0, released 2026-08-14)` is a **live claim about what is current, and it is now wrong**. Match the v16 entry's form.

⛔ **Item 4 is NOT in scope.** Whether *"a published version has no section on its per-major page"* should be mechanised is a real design question with an open answer; file it if you want it considered, ⛔ do not build it here.

## ⛔⛔ The single largest risk on this card: FABRICATION

You are writing **curated prose that ships to users on a public page**, about a release you did not make. The card is explicit and I am making it a ruling:

> I have not read the 69 changelog sections and I am **not** asserting what 17.1.0 should say.

⇒ **Every claim you write must be traceable to what actually shipped.** The sources of truth are the **69 package `CHANGELOG.md` sections under `## 17.1.0`** and the changesets they were compiled from — ⛔ not the issue tracker, ⛔ not your expectations of what a minor "usually" contains, ⛔ not this comment.

- `packages/cli`'s `## 17.1.0` section alone is **866 lines**. Read the material; do not sample it and generalise.
- If a change is user-facing but you cannot establish what it does from the changelog entry, ⛔ **leave it out** rather than describing it plausibly. An omission is recoverable; a false sentence on a release page is what #10229 is a card about.
- The card verified exactly **two** user-facing items in the published tarball — #9736 (`init` scaffolds declare `sharingModel`; `scaffold-validate` runs the same rule set `dev` reaches) and #9347/#8978 (the ready banner's `Config:`/`Artifact:` row names what actually booted) — and calls them *"two data points, not a survey"*. ⚠️ Treat them as confirmed anchors, ⛔ not as the outline.

## ⛔ Release-act fence

The publish **already happened** (`@objectstack/cli@17.1.0`, `2026-08-20T11:21:17.400Z`). You are documenting it, not performing it. ⛔ Do NOT run `changeset publish` / `pnpm run release`, push a tag, cut a GitHub Release, or `workflow_dispatch` any publish-capable workflow. ⛔ Do NOT modify the root `version` script chain. If you find evidence the release ran without a human, ⛔ do not "repair" it — **report it** and it becomes an incident for the maintainer.

## PM 机制假设 (measure — falsifying these is a good run)

⚠️ **The shared working checkout is STALE** at `9ff11921a` with `packages/cli` still 17.0.0 — the card says so explicitly and it will mislead you. Read `origin/main` via `git show origin/main:<path>`. Depth-50 shallow clone ⇒ ⛔ `git log` lies about file history.

- `npm view @objectstack/cli dist-tags` → `latest: 17.1.0`; `packages/cli/package.json` on `origin/main` is `17.1.0`.
- 69 package CHANGELOGs carry a `## 17.1.0` section.
- The v17 page's heading spine ends at the rc.6 "Landed since" blocks — nothing for 17.1.0.

**Re-derive all of it.** If the count is not 69, or a section already exists, that is the finding.

## Acceptance criterion

Every substantive claim in the new section **traceable to a named CHANGELOG entry or changeset** — say in your report how you established the section's contents and what you deliberately left out. ⛔ "It reads like a plausible 17.1.0" is not a criterion; "each line has a source" is.

⚠️ Downstream consumer, so accuracy is not cosmetic: `objectstack-ai/objectos` mirrors this content and links readers to `/docs/releases/v17` for the full notes. **Two doc sites currently tell readers 17.0.0 is current, six days after it stopped being.**

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` with **no path args**; run every family it names and quote each verdict line. `skip-changeset` expected (docs-only) — judge from your diff.

**Final report**: structured JSON, returned AND posted here with first line `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. ⚠️ Sanitizer has eaten that marker three times today — read your comment back and add a literal fallback if stripped.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #10271

Reviewed against GitHub and against `origin/main`, not against the report. All 23 checks green (`Test Core` / `Dogfood` correctly *skipped* by the docs path filter; `Build Docs`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Spec property liveness` all pass). Flipped ready, auto-merge armed.

### What I re-derived myself

**1. The extraction reproduces exactly.** Independently walking `origin/main`: 78 `CHANGELOG.md` files, **69** carrying a `## 17.1.0` section, **25,037** section lines. Both numbers match the report to the digit — which is the thing that makes the rest of the arithmetic (314 entries / 312 hashes / 111 minor / 203 patch) worth trusting rather than just plausible.

**2. The anchor correction holds, and the control fires.** This is the claim I cared most about, because it is the dev contradicting the card I wrote:

| number | hits in the 69 sections |
|---|---|
| `#8978` | 1 ✅ |
| `#8985` | 1 ✅ |
| `#9666` | 1 ✅ |
| `#9736` | **0** — and 0 even as bare digits |
| `#9347` | **0** — and 0 even as bare digits |

The three "should be present" numbers are the positive control; a zero-hit result means something only because they return non-zero from the same command. `#99999` returns 0 as the negative control. **The card's #9736 and #9347 do not exist in the 17.1.0 train and my card was wrong to cite them.**

**3. The behaviours are real, which is the harder half.** I read the full entry bodies rather than trusting the one-line index:

- `10bbc19` (#9666) — *"`objectstack init` scaffolds now compile — templates author an OWD, and the scaffold self-test runs the author-time rules"*. That is verbatim the behaviour my card described under the wrong number.
- `49dba54` (#8978) — and here the report is *more* right than it claims. I expected the `Artifact:` half to need a separate anchor. It does not: the same entry adds *"an `Artifact: … (OS_ARTIFACT_URL)` row when `OS_ARTIFACT_URL` pinned one, omits the row on the other artifact-fallback paths"* alongside the `Config:` fix. One changeset, both rows. `#9347` was never needed.
- `14c9ad7` (#8985) — the `OS_ARTIFACT_PATH` child-environment change, correctly kept as *related to*, not conflated with, the banner fix.

**4. Every issue number in the new prose is traceable.** 119 distinct `#NNNN` in the 749 added lines; **0** absent from the 17.1.0 train, under a boundary-anchored match so `#4001` cannot be satisfied by `#40012`. That is the anti-fabrication ruling passing its own test rather than being asserted.

**5. Nothing was destroyed to make room.** The 11 deleted lines are exactly the three superseded claims — the old index bullet, the frontmatter description, the 9-line release-status blockquote. I read the replacement blockquote in full: the rc.0…rc.6 train, the `changeset pre exit` note, the caret-range explanation and the breaking-density rationale all survive inside it. No 17.0.0 content is lost, and the added `⚠️ 17.1.0 is a minor by version number, not by blast radius` paragraph is the right warning to attach to a minor that moves who can read and write.

### Two gates that went red first

Recording these because in both cases the gate caught something review would have waved through: `check:release-page-status` rejected *"17.1.0 is the current release"* on an end-anchored `releasedAssertionRe` — a sentence no human reader would call stale, which is precisely the case that gate documents itself as existing for. And `check:role-word`'s ratchet moved 2 → 3 on a "role" usage quoted straight out of a source changeset; ADR-0090 D3 bans new occurrences regardless of provenance.

### ⚠️ Correction to the PR body — mine to make, not the dev's

#10271's body opened with *"This is the sanctioned **dedicated docs-only PR** for that gap."* **That named the wrong channel.** `content/docs/releases/**` has exactly two: a *factual error* goes through a dedicated docs-only PR; a *completeness gap* goes through **per-card maintainer approval**. Authoring a missing section is a completeness gap, so this PR rides the second channel. The body's next paragraph already had it right and carried the verbatim approval — 「补写 17.1.0 章节 已经有issue，插队处理」 — so the body was self-contradictory rather than unauthorized. The work was always sanctioned; the citation was not.

I have rewritten the body so the warrant it records is the one it actually rests on, and stated explicitly that **no future PR may cite #10271 as licence to open a docs-only PR into `content/docs/releases/**`**. ⛔ Not a precedent.

### Carried forward

**#10268** (item 4 of this card, deliberately out of scope): `check:release-page-status`'s predicate is keyed on the *major*, so `17.0.0 is released` satisfies it while `latest` is 17.1.0 — which is why nothing flagged this page as stale for six days. Third occurrence of the class after #8917. Left unassigned; it is a gate-design card, not a docs card.
